sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Eclecticism**: The style is a **synthesis** of Chola, Hoysala, Pandya, and Chalukya traditions with **Indo-Islamic** influences (arches, domes, vaults).
• **Scale & Grandeur**: Shift from small shrines to **massive temple complexes** with multiple enclosures (Prakaras).
• **Materiality**: Predominant use of **hard granite** (local to Hampi) which necessitated bold, heavy carvings rather than delicate filigree.
• **Key Metric**: The **Rayagopuram** (monumental gateway towers) became the defining vertical element of the landscape.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Temple Urbanism**: Temples functioned as economic hubs, banks, and administrative centers.
• **Hydraulic Engineering**: Sophisticated tank systems (e.g., Kamalapuram tank) integrated with temple architecture.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Preservation of granite structures from weathering and historical vandalism.
• **Solutions**: UNESCO World Heritage site management and digital documentation of Hampi ruins.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'K-A-M-P' (Kalyana Mandapa, Amman Shrine, Monolithic Sculptures, Pillar Yali).
• **Decoded Meaning**: These are the four pillars of Vijayanagar architectural identity.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse Vijayanagar 'Yali' pillars with Hoysala 'Soapstone' carvings. Vijayanagar used granite, which is harder and less intricate than Hoysala soapstone.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Indo-Saracenic synthesis' to describe the secular architecture (Lotus Mahal) to demonstrate analytical depth.

keyTakeaways: Vijayanagar architecture is defined by the transition to massive granite structures and the Rayagopuram.
The style represents a unique blend of indigenous Dravidian traditions and Islamic structural elements.
Temple complexes were not just religious sites but central nodes of the Vijayanagar socio-economic and political system.
